title: SRE SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, and Runbooks - Standards & Playbook
author: Ari Chen
content:
Purpose

This document defines Redwood Inference's standards and playbook for service-level objectives (SLOs), error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, operational tooling, and runbook templates. It is intended for service owners, SREs, on-call engineers, and engineering managers.

Summary / Scope

- Applies to all public-facing Redwood API services (text-generation, chat, embeddings), internal control-plane services (routing, orchestration), and the Dedicated control plane.
- Primary goals: consistent SLO definitions, enforceable error-budget policies, repeatable capacity planning, and high-quality incident reviews/runbooks.

1) SLO Definitions & SLIs

Overview
- SLOs are statements of reliability customers can expect. Each SLO is backed by 1-3 SLIs (Service Level Indicators) and a clearly documented measurement window.
- Default measurement window: 30 days (rolling) for availability and latency SLOs; 7 days for operational indicators used in releases.

Required SLOs (per service)
- Availability SLO (customer-facing request success): 99.95% (target) measured on successful 2xx responses for API request classes.
- Latency SLOs (p95):
  - Interactive generation endpoints: p95 < 500 ms (small payloads)
  - Streaming/chat endpoints (initial response): p95 < 700 ms
  - Embeddings endpoints: p95 < 300 ms
- Error-free payloads (semantic correctness guardrails): 99.5% on curated eval prompt sets (applies to model-serving teams during rollout).

SLI Implementation Notes
- Use server-side request logs + tracing (OpenTelemetry) as primary source. Metrics aggregation must be tag-aware (route, model_version, region, customer_tier).
- Measurement must exclude planned maintenance windows and user-initiated retries above configured limits.

2) Error Budgets & Burn Policies

Definitions
- Error budget = (1 - SLO) * measurement_window. Example: for 99.95% availability, monthly error budget = 0.05% of requests.

Burn Policy (standard)
1. Low burn (< 10% of budget in 7d): monitor, no restrictions.
2. Moderate burn (10-50% in 7d): require incident RCA within 5 business days; postpone non-critical launches.
3. High burn (> 50% in 7d OR > 25% in 24h): immediate action: halt non-critical deploys, initiate war room, notify executive on-call.
4. Exhausted budget: emergency mitigation plan, capacity or design changes, and a mandatory postmortem and reliability plan with milestones.

Release and Rollout Controls
- All automated canary checks must include SLO-relevant SLIs. If canary consumes >10% of error budget within rollouts, rollback immediately.
- Feature flags and gradual percentage rollouts required for changes to model-serving or routing that affect latency or availability.

3) Capacity Planning Process

Goals
- Ensure capacity for 99th percentile peak demand + safety buffer to meet latency SLOs with 95% confidence.

Quarterly Capacity Planning Steps (owners: SRE + Infra Capacity team)
1. Demand forecast: use historical q95 request rate, new product launches, and sales pipeline commitments (data from Finance / Sales).
2. Workload characterization: breakdown by endpoint, model_family, sequence_length distribution, and customer_tier.
3. Performance envelope: use recent benchmark matrix (kernel/quantization profile) to translate QPS into GPU and memory demands.
4. Safety buffer: target 20% headroom on baseline for Hosted; 30-50% for Dedicated early-adopter pools.
5. Procurement & reservations: convert capacity need to cloud reservations or hardware procurement lead times.
6. Runbook update: update service runbooks with new capacity targets and scaling actions.

Autoscaling and Policies
- Autoscaler threshold recommendations (default): CPU utilization 60-75% for control-plane; GPU utilization (inference) 70-85% depending on model latency sensitivity.
- Batching targets: configure request batching to maintain SLOs-prefer deadline-based batching for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- Graceful degradation: configure routing policies that fall back to smaller/cheaper model variants under sustained high load instead of full denial of service.

Capacity Table (example columns)
- service_name | model_family | region | baseline_qps_p95 | expected_peak_qps_p99 | gpu_type | gpus_required | safety_buffer_pct | owner | procurement_date
- Example row: api-generation | redwood-2-small | us-west-2 | 1200 | 2200 | A100-80GB | 12 | 25 | eng-serving-runtime | 2027-02-01

4) Reliability Initiatives (OKR / Project cadence)

Types of initiatives
- Latency work: kernel selection, batching improvements, KV cache hit rate optimization.
- Cost/reliability tradeoffs: quantization profiles with explicit quality gates.
- Observability: new traces, synthetic customers, and per-model SLIs.
- Operational tooling: deeper autoscaler metrics, pre-warming tools, and runbook automation.

Initiative lifecycle
1. Proposal with impact estimate (SLO improvement, cost, implementation effort).
2. Approval by SRE council and product stakeholders.
3. Pilot in staging with synthetic workloads.
4. Gradual rollout and SLI monitoring.
5. Post-rollout measurement and handover to operations.

5) Incident Review Standards & Postmortems

Incident classification
- Sev 1 (P0): customer-visible outage violating availability SLO for > 15 minutes for multiple customers or major revenue-impacting degradation.
- Sev 2 (P1): significant degradation affecting a subset of customers or sustained increased error budget burn.
- Sev 3 (P2): partial impact, degraded performance within error budget bounds, or non-critical internal failures.

Postmortem requirements (timeline)
- Draft within 48 hours: preliminary timeline, detection, mitigation steps, and list of impacted services/customers.
- Final postmortem within 10 business days: root cause analysis, contributing factors, timeline, impact (quantified), action items with owners and due dates.
- Severity > P1 requires an external summary for customer-facing communications within 3 business days.

Action item standards
- Each action must have owner, due date (<= 90 days for medium-priority, <= 30 days for high-priority), and verification criteria.
- Aging policy: actions older than due date escalate to SRE manager and are reported in monthly reliability review.

Postmortem format (required sections)
1. Summary (1-2 lines)
2. Timeline (detailed)
3. Detection and mitigation steps
4. Root cause and contributing factors
5. Metrics/graphs (attach PR/links to dashboards)
6. Action items (owner + due date)
7. Lessons learned and follow-ups

6) Operational Tooling & Observability Standards

Logging and Tracing
- All services must emit structured request logs (JSON) with fields: request_id, route, model_version, region, customer_id_hash, latency_ms, response_code, cpu_ms, gpu_ms, batch_size.
- Distributed traces must include model invocation spans and kernel-level timings where available.

Dashboards and Alerts (required sets)
- Service overview: availability, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, traffic QPS, error budget burn rate.
- Capacity dashboard: current utilization by pool, queued requests, batch efficiency, and pre-warm status.
- Alert categories: P0/P1 (pager), P2 (email + slack), P3 (dashboard only).

Alert thresholds (examples)
- Availability: sustained 5-minute availability < 99.5% => P0 pager.
- Latency: p95 > SLO + 100ms for 5 minutes => P1 pager.
- Error budget burn: burn rate > 10% per day => P1.
- Queue depth: GPU request queue > 100 for 3 minutes => P1.

Synthetic Testing & Chaos
- Run synthetic user tests against production-read replicas hourly for critical flows.
- Quarterly chaos tests: pre-approved blast radius, required page on-call and product stakeholder notified.

7) Runbook Templates & Examples

Runbook structure (required)
- Title, service, owner, on-call rotation, contact list, runbook version, last updated.
- Symptoms (how incidents manifest).
- Impact assessment (customer classes affected).
- Immediate mitigation steps (stepwise, numbered).
- Diagnostic commands / dashboard links (include CLI examples).
- Root-cause remediation & long-term fixes.
- Rollback/restore procedures.
- Post-incident actions and follow-up checklist.

Example: High Latency on Generation Endpoint
1. Symptom: p95 latency for /v1/generate increases above 900ms and user complaints spike.
2. Impact: interactive chat customers experience slow responses; internal error budget burn increases.
3. Immediate mitigation:
   a. Verify dashboard: confirm p95 latency by region and model_version.
   b. Open tracer sampling for affected requests and inspect kernel timings.
   c. If GPU queue depth > threshold, scale up GPU pool (manual scale) or shift traffic to alternate region.
   d. If a recent deploy coincides with onset, roll back to previous model_version or routing config.
4. Diagnostics: run command
   - kubectl logs -l service=api-generation --since=5m | jq '.request_id, .latency_ms, .model_version'
   - Check autoscaler metrics: /dashboards/capacity
5. Remediation: tune batching deadline or reduce batch size for latency-sensitive routes; file initiative to improve batching heuristics.

8) Ownership, Governance, and Reporting

Roles & responsibilities
- Service Owner: defines SLOs, approves runbook changes, signs off on capacity needs.
- SRE Team: enforces SLO monitoring, triages incidents, maintains runbooks, executes capacity planning.
- Infra/Capacity: procurement, reservations, and autoscaler implementation.

Reporting cadence
- Weekly: error-budget burn report to SRE council (automated report).
- Monthly: capacity and utilization review with product and finance.
- Quarterly: reliability initiatives review (OKR sync) with execs.

9) Appendices

A. Measurement windows and exclusion rules
- Planned maintenance windows must be recorded in the maintenance calendar and excluded from SLO calculations if published 72 hours in advance and less than 4 hours in duration.
- Retry storms: define client-side retry limits and exclude retries beyond configured thresholds from SLO numerator/denominator.

B. Quick links (dashboards & runbooks)
- Service Overview dashboard: /dashboards/service-overview
- Capacity dashboard: /dashboards/capacity
- Runbook repository: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks
- Incident postmortem template: /confluence/eng-sre/postmortem-template

C. Change log
- 2026-10-10: Initial published standard combining SLOs, capacity planning, runbook templates, and incident review standards.

If you have questions or need a tailored SLO/capacity assessment for a specific service, tag @ari.chen on the SRE Slack channel (#sre-ops) or open a ticket in the reliability board.
